title: Customizations Entry Point
intro:
How should people find the Customizations modal in the Agents window?

In a recent A/B experiment (vscode-internalbacklog#10416), replacing the bottom-of-sidebar section that listed each customization type with a single "Customizations" button at the top of the sidebar cut Customizations opens by 45% and creation starts by 40%. The hypothesis: "Customizations" is an opaque term, while "Skills" and "MCP Servers" have well-known value.

These five options try to keep the cleaner, smaller footprint while still showing people which customization types exist. All are built on the latest Session Customizations direction (session-scoped right sidebar, global Customizations modal).

Try hovering and clicking the entry point at the top of the left sidebar (in the last option, the chips under the composer), then open a session and start a new one (⌘N). Please focus on the entry point itself, not the modal's contents.
questions: Which option best balances a clean, compact sidebar with making the customization types visible? Why?
Which option would most make you want to click in and explore Skills, MCP Servers, Agents, etc.?
Do any options feel noisy, distracting, or out of place in the Agents window?
For options with type links (hover card, chips), is jumping straight to a type more useful than opening the overview?

items.label: Inline types + hover card
items.note: One row: "Customizations" followed by a muted "Skills · MCP · Agents". Hover it for a card listing every type with counts; each links straight to that type.

items.label: Type chips
items.note: The Customizations row plus one line of small type chips underneath. Each chip opens that type; +N opens the overview.

items.label: Ticker
items.note: One row whose description cycles once through the types with counts (84 Skills → 8 MCP Servers → …) and then settles. Replays when you start a new session.

items.label: Named entry
items.note: Same single button as today, relabeled "Skills, MCP & more" instead of "Customizations".

items.label: Composer shortcuts
items.note: Today's sidebar button stays as is. On the new-session view, a dismissible row of type chips sits under the composer.
